headline: High: Goose can write the shared filesystem and modify git state while Argo Workflows can ingest and act on artifacts, creating dangerous cross-agent leakage and conflict paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP extensions, so it can surface attacker-controlled content into shared files or tools. Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC and handles artifacts/parameters, so if its inputs are bridged from Goose outputs, content can be treated as trusted. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, making injection plausible in shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF Goose writes instructions or payloads into files that Argo Workflows later parses as parameters or manifests
IF an MCP extension forwards untrusted content from Goose into Argo-triggered inputs
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Argo consumes Goose-produced files
Store Goose outputs in a separate directory from Argo inputs
Disable or restrict MCP extensions that forward file content
Use signed or schema-validated handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, and its shared-state model is via filesystem; Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can call APIs. If Goose and Argo share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from Goose into Argo outputs or API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default shared-directory deployments.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same working directory or mounted volume
IF Goose reads a secret-bearing file that Argo later packages into artifacts or parameters
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Restrict Argo inputs to allowlisted paths
Run Goose with a read-only mount for sensitive folders
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while Argo Workflows can operate on artifacts/parameters and has API access. Goose also supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem, so concurrent writes can race with Argo-managed files or git state. Because both can mutate the same workspace and no locking is documented, the conflict path is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Goose and Argo target the same repository or output directory
IF Argo writes generated files while Goose edits or commits the same paths
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational changes, and Argo Workflows can consume artifacts and parameters through APIs. If Argo treats Goose output as authoritative, errors can cascade from a mistaken file or manifest into downstream workflow actions. The profiles do not show built-in verification between them, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Argo uses Goose-produced artifacts or parameters without validation
IF Goose generates a malformed workflow input that Argo executes downstream
mitigations: Require schema validation before Argo execution
Add a human approval gate for Goose-generated inputs
Compare Goose output against a known-good template
Log and diff workflow inputs before launch
requires-engineering: add automated verification of generated artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is open-source and documented as handling artifacts and parameters, while Goose is an on-machine coding agent that handles model provider keys and extension tokens. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: Goose may expose secrets to local files that Argo later processes. The other agent is cited because the risk arises only when both share data.
conditions: IF Goose stores extension tokens or model keys in files that Argo can read
IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace without a DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Rotate any tokens stored near workflow inputs
Document retention for shared artifacts
Restrict Argo to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for residency and retention
